captions.detailed: An independent rear suspension (IRS) half-shaft assembly consisting of an inboard constant-velocity (CV) joint, a central drive shaft with protective rubber boots, and an outboard CV joint integrated with a wheel hub flange. The inboard coupling is colored dark grey/black, while the main shaft is a thin black rod flanked by ribbed black rubber bellows. The wheel hub assembly on the outboard end features a light grey cylindrical body terminating in a mounting flange with five protruding black wheel studs.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of an independent rear suspension (IRS) rear half-shaft assembly. It should feature a dark grey inboard CV coupling, a central black drive shaft with ribbed rubber boots, and a light grey outboard wheel hub with a mounting flange and five wheel studs.
captions.factory: Construct the assembly by defining three main parts: the inboard coupling, the central shaft, and the outboard wheel hub. Use Cylinder primitives of varying diameters and lengths to build up the stepped cylindrical sections of the CV joints and boots. For the wheel hub, combine a main cylinder with a larger, thin cylinder to act as the flange, and pattern five smaller cylinders around its face to represent the wheel studs. Connect these parts using continuous and revolute joints to simulate realistic rotational and angular articulation.
